The NFL season is coming into view, which means more NFL player props are being released each week. Most national sportsbooks have posted 2026 NFL Player Props for Rushing Touchdowns for the top running backs and some quarterbacks. In this article, I highlighted a bet I’ve already dropped in our Betting Discord and a couple of additional wagers I considered.

Wagering your hard-earned money in the summer and waiting more than half a year for bets to be settled isn’t the easiest pill to swallow. Make sure to shop around for the best lines and odds if you have access to multiple sportsbooks. ##### __{{Jonathan Taylor|RB|IND|21682}}__ (Ind) over 11.5 rushing touchdowns (+115, Caesars)

+ __Why I like the over__: Taylor is coming off an NFL-best 18 rushing TDs, which was the second time he ran for 18 rushing TDs to lead the NFL in rushing scores. He finished behind only Derrick Henry with 19 carries from inside the 5-yard line, and he totaled 34 total carries from that range in the last two seasons. The Colts were among the most run-heavy offenses from inside the 5-yard line, ranking 27th in pass rate over expectation (-10%) from that area of the field. JT is coming off an NFL-best 73.1% carry share, and he’ll once again face no competition for carries from DJ Giddens and Seth McGowan.

+ __Why I ultimately passed__: Taylor has run for 18 TDs twice in six seasons, but he’s never cleared 11.5 rushing TDs in his other four seasons. Indianapolis’ offense ran scorching hot through the first 10 weeks of the season, averaging 32.1 PPG, which would’ve topped the Rams’ 30.0 PPG for the league lead over the entire season. The bottom eventually fell out against a much tougher schedule and because of Daniel Jones’ season-ending injury. Indy’s offense could look more like the second half of the 2025 version with Daniel Dimes working his way back from an Achilles injury. Alec Pierce is also questionable for the start of the season, and the Colts traded Michael Pittman to Pittsburgh.

##### __{{Chuba Hubbard|RB|CAR|21691}}__ (Car) over 4.5 rushing touchdowns (+105, BetMGM)

+ __Why I like the over__: Hubbard no longer has to battle Rice Dowdle for carries and goal-line opportunities. The Panthers have two unproven options behind him in Jonathon Brooks, who’s appeared in just three games since November 2023 because of a pair of torn ACLs in the same knee. Trevor Etienne earned just 20 carries and 63 snaps during his rookie season, even with Brooks out of the picture. Carolina scored just 25.7% of its touchdowns on the ground last season, which should regress this season after 45% of their TDs came via the ground in 2024. The Panthers easily led the league with a 16.4% pass rate over expectation from inside the 5-yard line last season.
+ __Why I ultimately passed__: The Panthers finished with the second-fewest rushing TDs (9) last season, and Hubbard had just 1 carry from inside the 5-yard line compared to 6 chances for Dowdle. The Panthers didn’t use him at the goal line last season, and he scored just once on 134 carries (.7%) overall. He couldn’t score from distance because he was the only RB who failed to break a single 15-yard run in a full season during the Fantasy Points Data era (2021-25) among RBs with 100+ carries in a season. Brooks, a 2024 second-round pick, has generated buzz early in the summer, with *The Charlotte Observer*’s Mike Kaye [writing](https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/nfl/carolina-panthers/article315949969.html) that Hubbard could cede more work to Brooks as the season moves along if he proves capable of handling it.

##### __{{Isiah Pacheco|RB|DET|23371}}__ (Det) under 4.5 rushing touchdowns (-118, BetMGM); __{{Jahmyr Gibbs|RB|DET|23200}}__ (Det) over 11.5 rushing touchdowns (+106, FanDuel)

+ __Why I like Pacheco’s under/Gibbs’ over__: Pacheco has scored just 2 rushing TDs on 214 carries in 23 games (postseason included) over the last two seasons. Pacheco couldn’t even keep the washed-up Kareem Hunt off the field in goal-line situations. The Chiefs didn’t give him a single carry from inside the 5-yard line last season, opting to give Hunt 13 opportunities from that same range. That bodes well for Gibbs, who has scored 10+ rushing TDs in each of his first three seasons, including 29 rushing scores in the last two seasons. Pacheco had to settle for a short-term deal for just $1.8 million guaranteed because of his declining play and his lack of pedigree. He’ll compete for snaps and touches as a distant #2 option behind Gibbs, whom Dan Campbell dubbed the team’s bell-cow back during OTAs.
+ __Why I ultimately passed__: Pacheco is looking to return to his form from 2022-23, and he’ll be nearly 22 months removed from a broken fibula at the start of the season. He averaged 4.71 YPC and 2.86 YACO/ATT with a 5.1% explosive run rate in his first two seasons before the injury, compared to 3.84 YPC and 1.94 YACO/ATT with a 1% explosive run rate in the last two seasons. He’s moving to a more prolific offense in Detroit that’s been one of the best at converting goal-line rushing TDs. The Lions scored the seventh-most rushing TDs (21) in 2025, the second-most (29) in 2024, and the most (27) since Gibbs arrived. Pacheco is looking to take over most of the role left behind by David Montgomery, including the eighth-most inside the 5-yard line carries (14) from last season.

##### __{{Kenneth Walker|RB|KC|19528}}__ (KC) over 6.5 rushing TDs (-110, Bet365)

\>Risk 1.1 units to win 1 unit. [Placed June 11](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/betting/2026/brolleys-best-bets-nfl-futures#/).

The Chiefs pried Walker away from the defending Super Bowl champions, handing him $28.7 million in guaranteed money over three seasons. That kind of money suggests __Andy Reid__ will use Walker as a featured back after KWIII split duties with __Zach Charbonnet__ in Seattle. Charbonnet dominated Walker in goal-line opportunities, leading him in rushing TDs (12>5) and inside the 5-yard line carries (16>7). It was the first time KWIII failed to reach 7+ rushing touchdowns in his fourth season, but he scored 4 rushing TDs in the postseason once he became the lead back because of Charbonnet’s season-ending injury. The Chiefs moved on from __Isiah Pacheco__ and __Kareem Hunt__, who left behind 13 carries and 7 rushing TDs from inside the 5-yard line last season. I’d be surprised if Walker lost significant goal-line opportunities to the likes of __Emari Demercado__, rookie __Emmett Johnson__, and __Brashard Smith__.

Walker will get more opportunities around the goal line, and he’s shown the ability to score from anywhere on the field. Kansas City ranked 21st with 38 offensive touchdowns last season, thanks in part to their inability to create long runs. The Chiefs finished ahead of only the lowly Raiders in explosive run rate (2.6%), who finished with the NFL’s fewest TDs (25). Walker ranked behind only __De’Von Achane__ in explosive run rate at 6.8% last season, and he has the sixth-most explosive yards (1261) since entering the league in 2022. Walker has scored 51.6% of his touchdowns from 10+ yards away (16 of 31) since entering the league. For perspective, just 28.2% of rushing touchdowns came from 10+ yards away (144 of 510) across the NFL last season.

full_text:
The NFL is in “Phase Three” of the offseason, the final stage before contact practices begin with training camp in late July. We’ve seen a steady stream of news since OTAs (organized team activities) started in mid-May, and it always gets a little more interesting in June when veteran players are required to report for one mandatory minicamp unless they have an excused absence.

I went team by team to round up the most important fantasy headlines coming out of all 32 workouts. I’ll update this article through June 18, the final day of team activities in Phase Three. Check back often for regular updates!

\>Each news item will have a date at the end of it for when it was updated or added to the article…ADP data used in this article is based on the last month of drafts with our partners over at [Underdog Fantasy](https://www.fantasypoints.com/underdog#/)…Subscribe to our [Fantasy Bundle Package](https://www.fantasypoints.com/plans#/) to take your NFL research to the next level!

{{CTA|Underdog|omit=\[none\]}}

June 12
-------

##### __Free Agent__

+   __Stefon Diggs__ won’t be suspended for violating the league’s personal conduct policy, which comes five weeks after he was found not guilty of assaulting his private chef. He could strike a deal with a new team in the near future since he avoided a suspension. Diggs facilitated __Drake Maye__’s second-year breakout by ranking second in catch rate (85%), eighth in YPRR (2.53), and eighth in 1D/RR (.127) among 76 WRs who saw 50+ targets. The only thing that limited him from finishing higher than the WR24 (12.4 FPG) was his career-worst 55% snap share and a 65.4% route share. He never dipped below a 77% snap share in his first 10 seasons and a 78.4% route share in the Fantasy Points Data era (2021-25). The Patriots upgraded their diva WR spot by trading for __A.J. Brown__ on June 1, which takes them out of the running for Diggs. The Chiefs, Ravens, and Rams make the most sense if Diggs is looking to compete for a Lombardi Trophy at 33 years old. The Commanders, Raiders, Colts, and Giants are the other top options if he’s looking for playing time to pad his career numbers. Diggs’ ADP (133, WR54) is extremely reasonable for the time being, and it’s likely to surge as soon as he signs with a new team. *(Added June 12)*

##### __Tampa Bay Buccaneers__

+   GM __Jason Licht__ [said](https://www.tampabay.com/sports/bucs/2026/05/16/bucky-irving-kenneth-gainwell-sean-tucker-rachaad-white-zac-robinson/) in May that __Bucky Irving__ would be limited during OTAs but should be ready for training camp. HC __Todd Bowles__ was more pessimistic about Bucky’s timeline than Licht, telling the media a week later that he expected Bucky back in the summer *or fall*. Licht gave us better information as Irving participated in individual drills at a June 11 OTA practice. He suffered a left shoulder injury in Week 4 last season and missed seven straight games due to the issue and an ankle injury. He never regained his form even when he returned to the lineup, and he needed [offseason surgery](https://www.joebucsfan.com/2026/02/bucky-irving-had-offseason-shoulder-surgery/) to repair the lingering shoulder issue. Irving mentally struggled to get over his first major injury, and it shouldn’t be a huge surprise that the Buccaneers are taking it slow with Irving at this time of year. The Buccaneers paid __Kenneth Gainwell__ $9.83 million guaranteed to be a high-end #2 option behind Tampa Bay’s 2024 fourth-round pick. Gainwell has a history of earning a bigger role than expected, and this backfield is setting up to be a potential three-man committee. Bucky was already a tough click since he could be a between-the-20s player, with Gainwell stealing passing-game snaps and __Sean Tucker__ vulturing goal-line opportunities. He’ll be an even tougher click with his availability for the start of the season a bit up in the air, even with his ADP (53, RB22) sliding the last few weeks. Gainwell’s ADP (105, RB35) has gained plenty of steam, but he’s still the better pick even with his surge in price. *(Updated June 12)*

##### __Kansas City Chiefs__

+   __Xavier Worthy__ has been working out in a non-contact yellow jersey during Kansas City’s OTAs as he continues to recover from [offseason surgery to repair a torn labrum](https://x.com/MattFosterTV/status/2060042663584264501?s=20) in his shoulder. He initially suffered the injury just three plays into the regular season on a crossing route, which forced him to miss three games and labor through the rest of the season. Reid said at the NFL’s annual meetings that they limited his routes to protect him after his injury. He ran 39 mid/deep crossing routes (10.2%) and 17 shallow crossing routes (4.5%) on 381 total routes last season, compared to 55 mid/deep crossing routes (11.4%) and 41 shallow crossing routes (10.8%) on 481 routes as a rookie. Reid [told the media](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7351929/2026/06/12/chiefs-minicamp-xavier-worthy/) that Worthy has had a nice camp and is noticeably stronger entering his third season — he played at 5’11”, 165 pounds last season. A healthy Worthy is an excellent pick for some positive regression at his ADP (101, WR46), which is significantly reduced from his fourth-round ADP in 2025. He has some real upside considering __Rashee Rice__’s legal issues and __Travis Kelce__’s declining play entering his age-37 season. *(Updated June 12)*

##### __Washington Commanders__

+   __Jacory Croskey-Merritt__ sat out Washington’s three-week OTA on-field workouts because of a soft-tissue injury, and his availability for mandatory minicamp is up in the air. JCM has lost a little ground trying to carve out a bigger role in one of the NFL’s most wide-open backfields heading into training camp. He has the inside track for now to be the team’s lead runner, but he must hold off the likes of __Rachaad White__, __Kaytron Allen__, __Jerome Ford__, and __Jeremy McNichols__. White has 40+ receptions in each of his first four seasons, and I’ve preferred drafting him at his slightly higher ADP (117, RB37) over Croskey-Merritt (121, RB40) because of his receiving ability, but this is setting up to be an annoying fantasy backfield all season.

##### __Carolina Panthers__

+   The Panthers and __Jalen Coker__ agreed to terms on a three-year, $35 million extension, with up to $41 million in incentives. The UDFA out of Holy Cross was entering his final season under contract, but the Panthers wanted to lock up the former exclusive rights FA before he could test free agency next offseason. Coker picked up steam in deeper formats last summer, but his season got off to a painfully slow start. He missed the first six games for a quad strain, and it limited his production even when he did return. His season started to take off in Week 13, reaching 47+ receiving yards in five of his last six games, including a 9/134/1 receiving performance in a three-point loss to the Rams in the Wild Card Round. His upside is a bit capped with __Bryce Young__ at quarterback and __Tetairoa McMillan__ looking like a potential stud as a rookie, but he’s still a good pick at his ADP (135, WR55) as the #2 option in Carolina. *(Added June 12)*

June 11
-------

##### __New Orleans Saints__

+   __Chris Olave__ [said in late May](https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/chris-olave-ready-to-lead-new-orleans-saints-to-more-wins) that he had no setbacks from a blood clot in his lung, which forced him to sit out the season finale, and it took him a week to feel regular again. Olave still sat out team drills at mandatory minicamp, and __Kellen Moore__ [said](https://x.com/Matthew_Paras/status/2064745977668309148) he rested because he was still recovering from the blood clot. Olave is in negotiations with the Saints for a long-term contract, and both parties could be using the blood clot as an excuse to keep Olave from potentially picking up any unnecessary injuries before they agree to a deal. Olave has been putting in the work this offseason, either way, bulking up by 8 to 10 pounds after playing at a listed weight of 187 pounds. He admitted that he’s been on the smaller side for the position since he came into the league, and he said he put in extra work in the weight room to turn his size from a weakness into a strength. Olave dealt with multiple concussions earlier in his career, but is coming off a healthy campaign with a little extra weight added to his frame, which should theoretically help him to protect himself better. I’m buying into __Tyler Shough__ and __Kellen Moore__’s offense heading into Year 2. Olave is a player I’m targeting in the middle of the third round (28, WR11), especially if his ADP slides a bit because of the latest news. *(Updated June 11)*

##### __Carolina Panthers__

+   __Tetairoa McMillan__ has been in and out of practices this spring because of ongoing foot soreness, which started late in his rookie season. He didn’t miss any time because of the issue, and he hopes to be completely ready for training camp, but it’s still a bit concerning that the issue still hasn’t completely gone away. McMillan has still been able to put extra work in despite his foot discomfort, [adding 17 pounds](https://x.com/scott_fowler/status/2064779147138740238?s=20) of muscle to his 6’5” frame — he played at a listed 212 pounds last season. Tet’s ADP has been slipping in recent weeks before his foot concerns popped up, and he could dip below __Garrett Wilson__, __Emeka Egbuka__, and __Luther Burden__ leading up to training camp. *(Added June 11)*

##### __Philadelphia Eagles__

+   The Eagles are adapting to life without __A.J. Brown__ in early June, and they’ve been doing it without __Makai Lemon__, who missed the last two weeks of spring practices with a hamstring injury. Philly’s first-round pick was spotted with a [sleeve on his right leg](https://x.com/BrandonGowton/status/2061850732601508064?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw%7Ctwcamp%5Etweetembed%7Ctwterm%5E2061850732601508064%7Ctwgr%5Ed0f2e24745fa4e1a2a13c2fa332c5a8b1fa8b447%7Ctwcon%5Es1_c10&ref_url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.bleedinggreennation.com%2Fnews%2F176303%2Fmakai-lemon-injury-eagles-wide-receiver-reportedly-dealing-with-soft-tissue-issue) during OTAs. Second-round pick __Eli Stowers__ was also spotted with a sleeve on his right leg to finish up mandatory minicamp. The Eagles have no reason to push their rookies to practice right now if they’re dealing with minor issues, but it’s still something to file away if the issues pop up again in training camp or during the season. *(Added June 11)*

##### __Kansas City Chiefs__

+   __Patrick Mahomes__ participated in Chiefs OTAs on May 27, which was yet another sign that Mahomes is on track for the start of the season — he’s more than five months removed from ACL and LCL surgery in mid-December. The NFL gave it away that he’ll be ready for Week 1 when they scheduled the Chiefs to host the Broncos on Monday Night Football. I figured the schedule-makers would backload Kansas City’s primetime games and division contests just in case Mahomes was unable to play in the first month of the season. Instead, the Chiefs have one of their most important games on Monday Night Football in the season opener at Arrowhead Stadium. Mahomes [said on May 28](https://x.com/pgsween/status/2060065000408957095) that he’s working toward being fully cleared by the time training camp starts, but his recovery checkpoints run a week or two over the beginning of camp. The Chiefs see no long-term issues with Mahomes after they signed him to a two-year extension, which will pay him $504.7 million through 2033. Mahomes’ ADP (90, QB11) has started to tick up, and his ADP will continue to rise if it continues to look like he’ll be ready for Week 1 — I’ll be passing on him at his rising price. __Rashee Rice__ is tough to trust to be available for a full season, and Mahomes’ career-best 5.2 FP as a runner will be unsustainable coming off a major knee injury. *(Updated June 11)*

##### __Seattle Seahawks__

+   __Mike Macdonald__ said in late May that __Tory Horton__ could return to team workouts by the end of spring workouts, but it didn’t happen. Macdonald [said on June 10](https://x.com/BradyHenderson/status/2064832199761993806) that he still believes Horton should return early in training camp “if not the start of it.” Horton suffered a season-ending shin injury in Week 9, and Macdonald said that Horton received some good news in late May that could accelerate his return. Horton looked the part as a fifth-round pick before his injury, scoring 5 receiving TDs on just 22 targets and a punt-return TD in eight games. He’ll battle __Rashid Shaheed__ and __Cooper Kupp__ for the limited WR available behind __Jaxon Smith-Njigba__. Horton is off the fantasy radar to open the season and a player to stash on dynasty benches. *(Updated June 11)*

+   __A.J. Barner__ [revealed](https://x.com/BradyHenderson/status/2062670865154838902) that he underwent two surgeries after Seattle’s Super Bowl run for a pair of undisclosed injuries. He’s yet to miss a game in his two-year career, but he played through multiple ailments and finished on the injury report in Week 10 with a calf issue. He said he’s feeling better but will be ready to go for training camp. Barner’s situation is one to monitor in case he falls behind in his recovery, which would open up more opportunities for __Elijah Arroyo__. However, Arroyo is dealing with his own undisclosed issue and is not practicing at mandatory minicamp. He landed on the injured reserve for a knee injury late last season before returning to play 19 snaps in the Super Bowl. *(Updated June 11)*

June 10
-------

##### __Green Bay Packers__

+   __Matt LaFleur__ [told the media](https://packerswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/packers/2026/05/27/packers-tucker-kraft-injury-update-training-camp/90279476007/) in late May that __Tucker Kraft__ should be back to practice for the start of training camp or shortly thereafter. Kraft tore his ACL in Week 9 last season, and it appears he’s well on his way to being 100% after he [posted a video](https://x.com/LilySZhao/status/2057837118601167117?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw%7Ctwcamp%5Etweetembed%7Ctwterm%5E2057837118601167117%7Ctwgr%5E3479add276907f364b79eb4a091fe24433d2f81f%7Ctwcon%5Es1_c10&ref_url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.usatodaynetworkservice.com%2Ftangstatic%2Fhtml%2Fspac%2Fsf-q1a2z3584c02f3.min.html) of himself working out on May 22. He [told reporters](https://x.com/ByRyanWood/status/2064774613968794082?s=20) on June 10 that he expects to play in Week 1 without a snap count, but he anticipates starting training camp on the PUP list. Kraft was in the midst of a breakout season before his injury, ranking as the TE4 (14.6) overall and leading all receivers in YAC/REC (10.66). He surged up draftboards (82, TE5) in May as it appears he’ll be ready to play for all or most of the season. *(Updated June 10)*

##### __Washington Commanders__

+   __David Blough__ said after he was hired as the offensive coordinator that he wanted to get __Terry McLaurin__ [10 targets a game](https://www.wusa9.com/article/sports/nfl/washington-commanders/commanders-terry-mclaurin-targets-david-blough-offense-jayden-daniels-laremy-tunsil/65-0de571f4-4779-435a-bf0f-a4f09972b2f8). McLaurin said in mandatory minicamp that he’s being used all over the field and on a variety of different route combinations in Blough’s new offense, which is going to use more under-center and play-action calls. McLaurin [said](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7347152/2026/06/10/commanders-new-offense-jayden-daniels/?unlocked_article_code=1.pFA.s_ET.JpI3fuuBvcGo&source=athletic_user_shared_gift_article_twitter&smid=tw-share-ta), “I think the multitude of formations and route combinations is going to give all of us flexibility to move around the formation, keep the defense on their toes, and have a lot of routes that may look similar at the stem but different at the top. I love that because that allows me to present the same stem to these DBs, but they have to respect (that) I can go left, right, I can go vertical because I can still run by you, I could stop, or I could go in. Just having those types of variations in your route tree is just an unbelievable weapon to have as a receiver.” McLaurin saw 10 or more targets just four times over 27 games in the last two seasons. He played in just 10 games last season because of a quad injury, mustering just a WR35 (11.4 FPG). The Bills notably picked up his fifth-year option this spring, which is a sign that they could have bigger plans for him. It seems unlikely that __Joe Brady__ changes his approach at TE as he moves from offensive coordinator to head coach. It’s still worth taking a shot on Kincaid at his depressed ADP (131, TE13) because he has top-five potential at the position if he could ever get close to a 70% route share. *(Updated May 21)*

##### __Las Vegas Raiders__

+   ESPN’s Ryan McFadden believes the expectation is for __Kirk Cousins__ to open the season as the starting quarterback over first overall pick __Fernando Mendoza__. It’s not a big surprise, but Cousins received all of the first-team reps at early OTAs, while Mendoza worked mostly with rookies behind __Aidan O’Connell__. Mendoza will be watching from the sidelines in September if minority owner __Tom Brady__ has as much influence as it seems from the outside. Brady previously called it a “[tragedy](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/zyclRMckosM?sttick=0)” to force rookie quarterbacks to play early in their careers. The Raiders will pay $11.3 million guaranteed to Cousins to mentor Mendoza this season, which is a starter’s salary and makes him the 20th-highest-paid QB in average annual value. The bigger question is when Mendoza will enter the starting lineup. The Raiders don’t have any obvious on-ramps to get Mendoza in the lineup because all of their games are on Sunday, and their bye week doesn’t arrive until Week 13. Mendoza is off the radar in redraft leagues and a player to stash in 2-QB/Superflex formats to open the season. Cousins is a QB3 option for at least September in 2-QB/Superflex leagues. *(Added May 21)*

##### __Pittsburgh Steelers__

+   The Steelers and __Aaron Rodgers__ finally came to terms on a one-year, $22 million guaranteed deal that is worth up to $25 million. He said on May 20 that this upcoming season would be his last, but he admitted he thought 2025 would be his final season after __Mike Tomlin__ stepped away before being drawn back in by the Steelers' hiring __Mike McCarthy__. Rodgers wanted the ball out of his hands last season, finishing with the fastest average time to throw (2.38 seconds) and the fourth-lowest aDOT (6.3 yards) among 45 QBs who attempted 100+ passes. The style of play led him to rank 10th in catchable throw rate (76.9%) and fourth in turnover-worthy throw rate (1.6%), but 31st in hero throw rate (3.8%). He’s posted a solid 4.8% TD rate in each of his last three healthy campaigns, but he’s unlikely to do much better at 42 years old. The Steelers at least added __Michael Pittman__ and __Germie Bernard__ to a receiving corps that ranked 31st in 11 personnel (38.9%) under playcaller __Arthur Smith__. Rodgers will step into a familiar offense under his longtime Packers HC, whose offense ranked ninth in 11 personnel (70.8%) in his final season with the Cowboys. Rodgers won two of his four MVPs under McCarthy, but those days are long gone. He should at least have a little more upside than his QB27 (14.7) from last season, with a better receiving corps around him. *(Updated May 20)*
